decision.question: Should customer upsert happen in pre-check phase or inside the main transaction?
decision.rationale: Pre-check customer upsert would be a separate DB call. If the transaction later fails, the customer row is orphaned with no record pointing to it. Keeping it inside the transaction ensures atomicity — matching how del-by-id.ts handles everything in one COMMIT.
decision.alternatives: Pre-check phase (separate DB call before transaction)

decision.question: Migration-42 uses customer_id FK on records, but types have record_customer_name/record_customer_phone. Which approach?
decision.answer: Upsert customers table, use customer_id FK
decision.rationale: Migration-42 is the authoritative schema. The type definition is outdated.
decision.alternatives: Insert name/phone directly (matches old type definition)

decision.question: When a capital row exists with matching capital_capital, how should stock be updated?
decision.rationale: Standard inventory behavior. Matches how del-by-id.ts computes undo stock.

decision.question: When product.id is undefined (new product), should we INSERT into products + product_codes?
decision.answer: Yes — always INSERT into products and capitals. Only INSERT into product_codes if product.code.length > 0.
decision.rationale: Transaction should be self-contained. New products must be created before capitals and product_events can reference them. Codes are optional for new products.
decision.alternatives: Require at least one code; Products always created elsewhere first

decision.question: product_event_type is commented out in migration-42. Omit from INSERTs?
decision.rationale: Column was removed in migration-42. Confirmed commented out in schema and types.

decision.question: Must new products have at least one code? Can existing products have empty codes?
decision.answer: Codes are always optional for both new and existing products.
decision.rationale: Product can exist without scannable codes. Product management screen can add codes later.
decision.alternatives: Require at least one code for new products

decision.question: Should we validate product.qty > 0?
decision.answer: Yes — yield InvalidQuantity error listing product indices with qty <= 0.
decision.rationale: Zero or negative qty is meaningless; would create no-op product_event_value of 0.

decision.question: What if a single product has duplicate codes (e.g., ["ABC", "ABC"])?
decision.answer: Silently deduplicate per product before collision checks.
decision.rationale: Duplicate within same product is harmless for business logic but would hit PK constraint on INSERT. Better to fix silently.

decision.question: How should validation errors be structured?
decision.answer: Five separate error classes with typed payloads: EmptyTransaction, InputCodeCollision, DbCodeCollision, CodeMismatch, InvalidQuantity.
decision.rationale: Each error carries distinct typed payload. Typed errors enable the UI to handle each case differently.

errors.error: Same code used by 2+ products within request. Payload: { code, fromIdx, toIdx }[].
Code exists in DB for different product. Payload: { code, incomingProductIdx, existingProductId }[].
Existing product's incoming codes are NOT a subset of its DB codes. Payload: { productIdx, code }[].

decision.alternatives: Single Validation class with generic msg/details payload

decision.question: What exactly is a CodeMismatch?
decision.answer: For existing products: incoming codes must be a SUBSET of the DB codes. If product has codes ["A","B"] in DB and incoming sends ["A","C"], then "C" is a mismatch. Incoming ["A"] alone is fine (subset). DbCodeCollision takes priority — check collision first, then mismatch.
decision.rationale: Allows partial code submission without requiring all codes to be present. Collision is the more serious error.
decision.alternatives: Exact match required; all incoming codes must exist in DB

decision.question: What product_note for newly created products?
decision.answer: Empty string (''). Set later via product management screen.
decision.rationale: product_note is NOT NULL in schema but TxRecord input has no note field.
decision.alternatives: Add note field to TxRecord input

decision.question: What value for product_event_note?
decision.rationale: Simple, consistent, provides context without repeating product name (already in record_product).

If no matching capital: generate capital_id, push INSERT INTO capitals
Generate event_id, push INSERT INTO product_events (value, note as above)
Generate record_product_id, push INSERT INTO record_products
